I'll think this through like the farmer I am, then give the numbers.

---

**My thinking this season:**

I've been doing this 40 years. My land is 16.1 mu — I put 10 mu into the wheat-maize rotation like always, and keep 6.1 mu for cotton on the piece of ground that's a bit sandier and further from the well. Cotton doesn't like too much water anyway.

For wheat, I already planted in October. Now it's green-up time. Last year I got about 480 kg/mu, the year before maybe 500. I'll do what I did before — one bag of compound fertilizer (45% total, about 50 kg) per mu as base before planting, then two bags of urea (50 kg) split across green-up and jointing top-dressing. That comes out to around 27 kg of N per mu. The agro-shop owner told me years ago I could cut back, but my neighbor tried cutting urea and his wheat looked yellow in May, so I don't risk it. I'll irrigate 4 times — winter water, green-up, jointing, grain-filling. Spray twice for aphids and powdery mildew, maybe a third time if wheat midge shows up.

For summer maize after wheat harvest in June, I use Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed — everyone around here does. I go no-till, just direct seed into wheat stubble. Apply compound at sowing and top-dress urea at the big trumpet stage. Total N about 20 kg/mu. Maize here yields 550-600 kg/mu if the rain is decent. Two irrigations from the well if July-August is dry. One spray for corn borer.

For cotton, I plant in late April. Cotton is more work and more pesticide — bollworm, aphids, spider mites. I'll spray 6 times. Fertilizer: compound at planting, urea at flowering and boll-setting. Cotton needs potassium for boll quality so I add potassium sulfate. Yield maybe 270 kg/mu seed cotton if weather holds. Cotton price is so-so these days, but I've grown it all my life and the ground is suited to it.

I plough before wheat planting, rotary till for cotton in spring, no-till for summer maize.
